definitions.gloss: last moment, eleventh hour, last-ditch situation
definitions.explanation: The very last possible moment before a deadline or decisive point. Often implies being pressed for time or backed into a corner.

examples.japanese: {土壇場|どたんば}でキャンセルされた。
examples.english: It was cancelled at the last minute.

examples.japanese: {土壇場|どたんば}になって{予定|よてい}が{変|か}わった。
examples.english: The plans changed at the eleventh hour.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{土壇場|どたんば}に{強|つよ}いタイプで、{締|し}め{切|き}り{直前|ちょくぜん}にいつも{力|ちから}を{発揮|はっき}する。
examples.english: She's the type who performs well under last-minute pressure and always delivers right before the deadline.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
Historically, {土壇場|どたんば} referred to the execution ground — a raised mound of earth ({土壇|どたん}) where beheadings took place. From this, it came to mean a situation of final desperation with no escape.

USAGE:
Very commonly used in everyday Japanese to describe last-minute situations. Frequently appears as {土壇場|どたんば}で (at the last moment) or {土壇場|どたんば}になって (when it came down to the wire).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {土壇場|どたんば}でキャンセル: last-minute cancellation
- {土壇場|どたんば}に{強|つよ}い: strong under pressure
- {土壇場|どたんば}の{決断|けつだん}: last-minute decision
- {土壇場|どたんば}に{追|お}い{込|こ}まれる: to be pushed to the brink
